American Bazaar, April 16, 2026 - Four Indian Americans among 2026 class of Guggenheim Fellows
caption:
He already holds India's highest literary honor. In April 2026, America gave him one of its own.

The Guggenheim Foundation named Amitav Ghosh to its 2026 Fellowship class on April 14, in general nonfiction - one of 223 Fellows named across 55 disciplines. Ghosh, based in Brooklyn, holds a PhD in Social Anthropology from Oxford and has spent decades writing on colonial history, migration and climate change. He already won India's Jnanpith Award in 2018 - the country's highest literary honor - and was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2024.

One writer, two countries' highest recognitions - the same body of work, judged worthy by both.
